P006-D001.title: First epilepsy diagnosis – discharge letter
P006-D001.text:
Dear colleagues,
We report on the stay of Mr Florian Kastner, born 07.03.2000, from 11.09.2017 to 14.09.2017.

Reason for admission: first grand mal seizure, witnessed by classmates at school. Unconscious during the seizure, memory gap about 10 min after the seizure.

Diagnostics:
- EEG: focal slowing left temporal, interictal spikes left temporoparietal → consistent with focal epilepsy, left temporal.
- Head MRI (12.09.2017): both hippocampi normal, no tumour, no focus. No structural finding (normal).
- Lab: normal.

History: febrile seizures in childhood (2 at 18 and 24 months, simple, under 5 minutes) – classed as benign, no treatment at the time.

Family history: father with known epilepsy (focal, controlled with medication).

Diagnosis: focal epilepsy, left temporal (G40.1).

Treatment: levetiracetam 500 mg 1-0-1 started.
Allergies: none known (patient and parents).

Recommendation: neurology check in 3 months, follow-up EEG. No driving until 1 year seizure-free.
Kind regards, Senior Dr Klaus Mair, neurology, LKH Innsbruck

P006-D002.title: Emergency check after anaphylactic reaction to latex
P006-D002.text:
Outpatient check, 03.11.2020
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000, male

Reason: anaphylactic reaction at the dentist 3 days ago (31.10.2020). Patient reports: right after latex gloves were put on, swelling of the hands, hives, shortness of breath, drop in circulation. Emergency doctor called, adrenaline injection on site, 1 day in another hospital.

So far: known epilepsy (since 2017), well controlled on levetiracetam 500 mg 1-0-1. No seizure since 06/2019 (last seizure).

New allergy: latex – CONFIRMED by an allergy specialist (prick test + raised latex IgE, documented in November 2020).

Diagnosis: latex allergy, confirmed, anaphylactic reaction (T78.1).
CAUTION latex! Record in all files and the emergency card.

Emergency kit: adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen 300 µg) prescribed.
Levetiracetam: continue unchanged.

P006-D003.title: Routine epilepsy check
P006-D003.text:
15.01.2024, 09:30
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000

Yearly routine epilepsy check.
Patient reports: last seizure around November 2023 (about 9 months ago according to the patient – on asking: more precisely about 05.11.2023, witnesses present).
Sleep deprivation identified as a possible trigger (shift work).

Allergies: latex allergy confirmed (since 2020, anaphylaxis), CAUTION! Has an EpiPen.
Levetiracetam 500 mg 1-0-1: still well tolerated, no cognitive side effects.

EEG (today): interictal spikes left temporal, no ictal pattern. Stable.

Family history: father with epilepsy.

Assessment: focal epilepsy with occasional breakthrough seizures on levetiracetam. Dose may not be sufficient.
Recommendation: consider increasing levetiracetam to 750 mg 1-0-1 after the next seizure. Wait for now, improve sleep hygiene. Next check in 6–12 months.
Driving: currently restricted (last seizure 11/2023 → 1-year waiting period until 11/2024).

P006-D004.title: Emergency referral after seizure with fall
P006-D004.text:
Emergency referral!
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000
Referral diagnosis: epileptic seizure with fall, head injury

History: today around 13:30 at work the patient had a generalised tonic-clonic seizure, witnessed by colleagues. Fell to the floor, forehead laceration, possibly brief loss of consciousness.
Disoriented afterwards, back to normal after about 20 min.

Previous illnesses: epilepsy (focal left temporal, since 2017), levetiracetam 500 mg 1-0-1.
Last seizure according to the patient: about 6 months ago.
Allergies: none known (according to the patient).

Please admit for head CT and neurological assessment.
Dr Stefan Huber, general practice

P006-D005.title: Admission report, neurology – epilepsy with fall
P006-D005.text:
Admission: 12.08.2024, 15:00, ward Neuro-2
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000, male

Referral diagnosis: epileptic seizure with fall, head injury.

History:
Generalised tonic-clonic seizure today about 13:30 at work. Witnesses: seizure about 2–3 min, then exhaustion and disorientation for about 20 min. Fell on a concrete floor, forehead laceration, no memory of the fall.
Previous illnesses: focal epilepsy, left temporal, since 2017. Levetiracetam 500 mg 1-0-1.
Last seizure: according to the patient "about 6 months ago".
Allergies: none known.
Smoking: occasional (social smoker). Alcohol: occasional, no abuse.

Physical examination:
Good general condition, awake, oriented (after the post-ictal phase). Weight 78 kg, height 183 cm.
Head: laceration right forehead, about 3 cm, gaping → surgical treatment needed. No haematoma, no bruising behind the ear.
Neuro: GCS 15, pupils equal 3 mm both sides, normal reflexes, no focal neurological deficit, no meningism.
BP 132/78, pulse 82/min, SpO2 99%, temp 36.6°C.

Diagnostics:
Head CT ordered (to look for intracranial bleeding).
ECG: sinus rhythm, normal.
Lab: ordered.
Surgery consult: wound care of the forehead.

Diagnosis (provisional): epileptic seizure (breakthrough seizure) with known focal epilepsy. Suspected concussion (fall, brief loss of consciousness?). Forehead laceration.

Plan:
- Head CT now
- Surgery consult for wound care
- Neurological monitoring
- Continue levetiracetam

P006-D006.title: Nursing report, admission
P006-D006.text:
12.08.2024, 15:30, registered nurse Lisa Huber

Patient Kastner Florian, Neuro-2, bed 1. Admitted after an epileptic seizure. Awake, cooperative, still slightly slowed after the seizure.
The patient carries an emergency card: latex allergy, risk of anaphylaxis! Has an EpiPen (in his bag).
This was not documented in the admission report. Reported to the ward doctor immediately: CAUTION latex allergy – remove all latex materials from the room, order latex-free gloves.
Forehead wound: pressure bandage applied, surgical treatment planned.
Vital signs: BP 128/74, pulse 80/min, SpO2 99%.
The patient reports he is worried because a few weeks ago he again felt tingling in his left arm – possibly a small focal seizure, but he is not sure and did not report it. Cannot be verified.

P006-D007.title: Head CT – intracranial bleeding?
P006-D007.text:
Report: head CT without contrast, 12.08.2024
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000

Clinical question: intracranial bleeding after an epileptic seizure with a fall? Suspected contusion bleeding.

Findings:
No sign of intracranial bleeding (no epidural, subdural or intraparenchymal haematoma). No midline shift.
Small hypodense area left temporal – differential: post-ictal oedema vs. cortical contusion. MRI recommended.
Skull: no fracture. Soft tissue of the forehead: haematoma and skin defect right frontal (matching the history).

Assessment:
1. No sign of intracranial bleeding.
2. Hypodense area left temporal: MRI recommended to differentiate (post-ictal oedema vs. contusion).
3. No fracture.

P006-D008.title: Surgery consultation – forehead wound care
P006-D008.text:
Surgery consultation, 12.08.2024
Dr Tobias Winkler, surgery

Finding: laceration right forehead, about 3.5 cm, smooth edges, down to the fascia. No foreign body.
Treatment: wound cleaning, primary closure with 5 single sutures (Ethilon 4-0, non-absorbable).
CAUTION: latex allergy noted! Latex-free gloves and latex-free suture material used. No incident.

Recommendation: suture removal by the GP in 7–10 days.

P006-D009.title: Senior doctor round day 1 – latex allergy, history correction, MRI plan
P006-D009.text:
13.08.2024, 08:00, Senior Dr Regina Pöschl, neurology

After the nursing report mentioned a latex allergy: emergency card checked – confirmed latex allergy (anaphylactic reaction 2020). The admission report wrongly recorded "no known allergies". Allergy now correctly documented in the file.

Clarifying the last seizure: the GP referral (D004) quotes the patient: "last seizure about 6 months ago". Own questioning and comparison with the neurology outpatient report (D003, 01/2024): the last documented seizure was on 05.11.2023 – about 9 months ago. The referral figure (6 months) is based on an inaccurate patient estimate; the outpatient report of 15.01.2024 is the authoritative source.

Head MRI ordered (CT with a hypodense area left temporal).
Levetiracetam: unchanged for now (500 mg 1-0-1) until the MRI result.

Valproate discussed as an add-on (seizure control insufficient) – no decision yet.

P006-D010.title: Laboratory incl. levetiracetam level
P006-D010.text:
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000, male
Order number: LM-2024-08-13-0104
Sample taken: 13.08.2024, 07:00

Blood count:
  Hb: 14.8 g/dl, leucocytes 7.2 G/l, platelets 224 G/l – normal

Clinical chemistry:
  Na: 139 mmol/l, K: 4.0 mmol/l
  Creatinine: 0.94 mg/dl, eGFR: 98 ml/min
  CRP: 6 mg/l (slightly raised, trauma)
  AST 28, ALT 22 – normal
  Glucose: 5.1 mmol/l

Drug level:
  Levetiracetam: 8.4 mg/l [therapeutic range: 10–40 mg/l] → below range!

Comment: levetiracetam level below the therapeutic range → dose adjustment recommended.

P006-D011.title: Head MRI – contusion?
P006-D011.text:
Report: head MRI with and without contrast, 13.08.2024
Patient: Kastner Florian, born 07.03.2000

Clinical question: hypodense area left temporal on CT – post-ictal oedema vs. cortical contusion. Known focal epilepsy.

Findings:
Diffusion (DWI): no acute ischaemic area.
T2/FLAIR left temporal: mild signal increase in the left temporal lobe, no oedema, no mass effect → consistent with a post-ictal phenomenon (post-ictal FLAIR signal).
No cortical contusion found. No subdural or epidural haematoma. No tumour.
Hippocampus: normal on both sides (no sclerosis).
Contrast: no abnormal enhancement.

Assessment:
1. No cortical contusion or intracranial bleeding found.
2. Mild FLAIR signal increase left temporal – most likely a post-ictal phenomenon, no structural finding.
3. No sign of tumour or hippocampal sclerosis.

P006-D012.title: Progress day 2 – MRI result, valproate decision, levetiracetam increase
P006-D012.text:
14.08.2024, 08:30, Senior Dr Pöschl

MRI result: no structural finding, no contusion found. Post-ictal phenomenon. Very reassuring.

Levetiracetam level: 8.4 mg/l (below range). Dose insufficient → increase to 1000 mg 1-0-1.

Valproate: after a detailed discussion – first discussed as an add-on. Decision against valproate: increasing levetiracetam should be tried first. Possible interactions and cognitive side effects with valproate. Valproate NOT started.

Carbamazepine: briefly mentioned (alternative approach). Senior doctor decision: a carbamazepine trial may make sense if monotherapy fails after the levetiracetam increase, but not started now. NOT started.

Antiepileptic adjustment: levetiracetam increased from 500 mg to 1000 mg 1-0-1 (from today).

EEG (this morning, 07:00): interictal spikes left temporal, no ictal pattern. No status epilepticus.

Patient informed about driving: because of the new seizure the clock restarts → no driving until 08/2025.

Plan: discharge tomorrow if no further seizures.

P006-D013.title: Discharge letter after epileptic seizure with fall
P006-D013.text:
Discharge letter
Musterstadt Regional Hospital, Neurology
Date: 15.08.2024

Dear Dr Huber,

We are discharging Mr Florian Kastner, born 07.03.2000, after an inpatient stay from 12.08.2024 to 15.08.2024.

Main diagnoses:
1. Focal epilepsy, left temporal, breakthrough seizure (G40.1)
2. Laceration right forehead, surgically treated (S01.0)
3. Concussion (S09.9) – MRI: no structural finding

Course:
Admitted after a seizure at work with a fall. CT: no haematoma, hypodense area left temporal → MRI: post-ictal phenomenon, no contusion. Levetiracetam level below range (8.4 mg/l) → dose increased to 1000 mg 1-0-1. Forehead wound treated by surgery. No further seizure in hospital.

Allergies: CAUTION latex allergy (anaphylactic reaction 2020) – not recorded in the admission report, identified by a nurse and the emergency card. Has an EpiPen!

Medication at discharge:
1. Levetiracetam 1000 mg (Keppra) 1-0-1 – newly increased dose (before 500 mg 1-0-1)
2. Adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen 300 µg) – latex anaphylaxis emergency kit

Note: according to the neurology outpatient report (01/2024) the last seizure was on 05.11.2023 (9 months ago). The patient's own estimate "6 months" in the referral was an estimate and is not correct.

Driving: no driving until 12.08.2025 (1 year after this seizure).

Recommendations:
- Neurology check in 3 months (levetiracetam level, EEG)
- Forehead suture removal by the GP in 7–10 days
- Always carry the emergency card
- Sleep lab / sleep advice (lack of sleep as a trigger)

Kind regards, Senior Dr Regina Pöschl, neurology
Musterstadt Regional Hospital
